situation: A cashier tells me my coupon expired and can't be applied to today's purchase.
behavior: I slam my hand on the counter, demand to speak to a manager, and use a sharp tone that makes other customers look over.

situation: On Saturday morning my partner suggests we go to our favorite coffee shop downtown
behavior: I pull the covers up and say 'you should go without me', then stare at the ceiling thinking everything feels pointless
affect: a heavy, low sadness that makes getting up feel impossible

situation: In a department meeting, my supervisor asks for a volunteer to lead the next client presentation.
behavior: I lower my eyes, sink into my chair, and hope someone else will step forward.
affect: My heart races and my stomach tightens.

situation: At the grocery store checkout, the cashier informs me the card reader is down and suggests I go to another register.
behavior: My hands start trembling, I struggle to respond, and I scan the store for escape routes while fighting back tears.
affect: Flooded, on the verge of tears

situation: A coworker reaches across the table and takes my pen without asking during a team meeting.
behavior: I sigh loudly, roll my eyes, and snap 'next time maybe ask first' in a sharp tone.

situation: My manager asks me to stay back after a group meeting to discuss a project.
behavior: I immediately assume I did something wrong and rehearse apologies while my hands get cold and shaky.
affect: I feel a rush of dread and my stomach drops.

situation: At a busy grocery store checkout, the cashier takes a long time to scan items.
behavior: I loudly tell the cashier to hurry up, my voice rising and my face turning red.

situation: When I arrive at the office kitchen each morning and see my coworkers chatting cheerfully.
behavior: I quietly set my coffee down, turn away, and sit alone at my desk, avoiding the chatter.

situation: I'm scrolling online late at night and see a sale notification for designer shoes
behavior: I enter my credit card details for the limited edition sneakers without checking my bank balance, then feel guilty when I see my account is overdrawn

situation: During a department meeting, my supervisor announces I need to present quarterly results to senior leadership tomorrow instead of the planned speaker.
behavior: I sit frozen, then quietly whisper to a coworker that I can't do this and ask if they'll take over, without offering any solution.

situation: I'm driving to a job interview when heavy traffic makes me realize I'll be at least 20 minutes late.
behavior: My hands shake on the wheel, I call to reschedule while catastrophizing that I've already ruined my chances.

situation: My roommate leaves their wet towel on the floor despite my having asked them to hang it up twice before.
behavior: I slam the bathroom door, text them a string of angry complaints, and refuse to speak to them for two days.

situation: During a team meeting, my boss praises my recent project publicly
behavior: I immediately interrupt to list three mistakes I made and apologize for them

situation: During a team lunch where a colleague proposes a fun trivia game where each person answers a personal question out loud.
behavior: I volunteer to refill everyone's drinks so I have an excuse to stay in the kitchen and avoid being called on.

situation: I'm at a friend's birthday dinner at a restaurant
behavior: I order multiple appetizers, finish my entree, and insist on ordering dessert and more drinks even after everyone else has asked for the check

situation: At a grocery store, I need to choose a cereal for my kids but can't decide and feel my hands start to shake.
behavior: I stand frozen in the aisle for over a minute, then leave without buying anything, overwhelmed by the responsibility of choosing wrong.

situation: My coworker asks me the same question for the third time during a team call.
behavior: I snap and tell them they should have been paying attention, then mute myself and exhale sharply.

situation: During a Sunday morning breakfast with my family, I am happily chatting when a minor frustration about a misplaced item triggers an abrupt shift to deep sadness.
behavior: I go from smiling and engaged to silent and withdrawn within minutes, excusing myself to lie down in my room while my family continues eating.

situation: At their partner's office holiday party, surrounded by strangers who keep approaching them
behavior: They stay near their partner the entire time, smile stiffly, and make excuses to refill their drink when colleagues start conversations

situation: I'm at a company pizza party with unlimited slices and my favorite toppings.
behavior: I eat seven slices even though I feel full and uncomfortably bloated, because I can't resist the abundance.
affect: Satisfied in the moment but vaguely guilty about my lack of control.

situation: After finding an unexpected $2,000 medical bill in their mailbox, they sit motionless on their kitchen floor for an hour, unable to open their laptop to look for payment plans.
behavior: Sits motionless on their kitchen floor for an hour, unable to open their laptop to look for payment plans

situation: A colleague unexpectedly asks me to share my weekend plans during a casual office lunch conversation.
behavior: I start explaining but lose my train of thought mid-sentence, repeat a word, and trail off while feeling my face get warm.

situation: At my annual performance review, my manager asks where I see myself in five years.
behavior: I stare at the wall, unable to name specific goals, then say 'I'm not really sure' and ask to move on to the next topic.
